part.text: [{"id":"R06401","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM inference is the protected workload; the security mechanism targets a gateway, not an LLM used for an OS-level security task.","evidence":"Third-party LLM gateways select providers, models, endpoints, and fallback paths"},{"id":"R06402","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM agents are the workload being isolated and migrated; no LLM performs security analysis on OS components.","evidence":"WebAssembly-based secure container framework that enables transparent live migration of LLM agent workspaces"},{"id":"R06403","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM-in-the-loop is used for benchmark tuning and synthetic interface verification, not an OS or privileged-interface security task.","evidence":"Benchmark Tuning with an LLM-in-the-loop"},{"id":"R06404","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"This is explicitly a survey, and reviews or surveys are excluded from the core empirical research set.","evidence":"This survey synthesizes the design space"},{"id":"R06405","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM appears only as a confidential inference workload; the security monitor composes cloud isolation, not LLM-driven OS security analysis.","evidence":"confidential LLM inference scenario"},{"id":"R06406","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM-backed agents are the entities being protected and revoked; the protocol is not an LLM used for OS security analysis.","evidence":"real LLM-backed agent swarms (GPT-4o-mini)"},{"id":"R06407","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"The work targets Web3 intent execution in a TEE; no LLM is used for an OS-level security task.","evidence":"TEE-based compiler that compiles intents into signed, state-bound transactions inside an enclave"},{"id":"R06408","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"A rogue agent is the threat being contained; the proposed protection is kernel-level preemption, not an LLM used substantively for the security task.","evidence":"Kernel-Level Preemption and Containment for Rogue Agentic Execution"}]
